ecodata

Overview

ecodata is an R data package developed by the Ecosystems Dynamics and Assessment Branch of the Northeast Fisheries Science Center for use in State of the Ecosystem (SOE) reporting. SOE reports are high-level overviews of ecosystem indicator status and trends occurring on the Northeast Continental Shelf. Unless otherwise stated, data are representative of specific Ecological Production Units (EPUs), referring to the Mid-Atlantic Bight (MAB), Georges Bank (GB), Gulf of Maine (GOM), and Scotian Shelf (SS). SOE reports are developed for US Fishery Management Councils (FMCs), and therefore indicator data for Scotian Shelf are included when available, but this is not always the case. ecodata has two companion bookdown documents: 1) Tech-Doc, which details the methods used in the SOE, and 2) the Northeast US Ecosystem Indicator Catalog, which provides expanded ecological context for SOE indicators. The ecodata package can be used to access to all of the indicators, datasets and plots featured in the SOE reports, which can be accessed using the table below. Please consult the technical documentation of SOE indicators before using data sets.

Year State of the Ecosystem: New England State of the Ecosystem: Mid-Atlantic
2020 State of the Ecosystem 2020: New England State of the Ecosystem 2020: Mid-Atlantic
2021 State of the Ecosystem 2021: New England State of the Ecosystem 2021: Mid-Atlantic
2022 State of the Ecosystem 2022: New England State of the Ecosystem 2022: Mid-Atlantic
2023 State of the Ecosystem 2023: New England State of the Ecosystem 2023: Mid-Atlantic
2024 State of the Ecosystem 2024: New England State of the Ecosystem 2024: Mid-Atlantic
2025 State of the Ecosystem 2025: New England State of the Ecosystem 2025: Mid-Atlantic

Installation

For the latest data and plots:

pak::pak("noaa-edab/ecodata")

For data used in the past, please replace “X.X.X” below with the desired ecodata version:

pak::pak("noaa-edab/ecodata@X.X.X")

Loading data sets

  1. All derived data sets are available once the package has been loaded into the environment. View available data sets using the syntax ecodata::...
